slot.brief: Given two 3D lines with a parameter, find the value of the parameter for which they intersect (or check coplanarity via determinant = 0).

stem: If the lines $x=1+u,\ y=-2+2u,\ z=3+3u$ and $x=p+2v,\ y=1-v,\ z=-1+v$ intersect, then $p$ equals

verdicts.working: Equating y and z coordinates gives 2u+v=3 and v=4+3u, so u=-1/5 and v=17/5. Equating x coordinates, 1+u=p+2v, gives p=-6.

working:
$A=(1,-2,3),\ B=(p,1,-1),\ \mathbf d_1=(1,2,3),\ \mathbf d_2=(2,-1,1)$. Since $(B-A)\cdot(\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2)=0$ and $\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2=(5,5,-5)$, $5(p-1)+15+20=0\Rightarrow p=-6$. The direction vectors are not parallel, so the coplanar lines intersect.

Independent check: Equating y and z coordinates gives 2u+v=3 and v=4+3u, so u=-1/5 and v=17/5. Equating x coordinates, 1+u=p+2v, gives p=-6.
solution:
For two non-parallel lines to intersect, they must be coplanar: $(B-A)\cdot(\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2)=0$.
$$\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf d_2=(1,2,3)\times(2,-1,1)=(5,5,-5)$$
With $B-A=(p-1,3,-4)$, $(p-1,3,-4)\cdot(5,5,-5)=0$, giving $5(p-1)+15+20=0$.
Hence $p=-6$.
